proposals.title: Chat hang: every queued link is bounded now, but abandoned work is not cancelled and nothing is measured
proposals.explanation: Operator report from live play: chat stops responding. Reading the code ruled out the first suspect. The controller serialises every message on `this.processing`, and every link is bounded by `withChatTimeout`: the message chain, the confirmation-deadline link and the priority controls. The deadline link used to append `expirePendingQuestion()` with no timeout, so a hang while resuming follow mode blocked every later message for good; it is now abandoned after one timeout, and since `expirePendingQuestion` clears all pending approvals before its only await, an abandoned expiry still fails closed. `status`, `stopp`, `hold`, `komm`, `komm zu mir` and `folge mir` bypass the queue, and queued work that has not started yields to them; `hilfe` answers at once. Every message is now timed - queue wait, handling, first reply, helper model - and logged, so a recurrence becomes a number. What remains: a timeout rejects without cancelling the work underneath, which keeps running and may mutate state later; and the operator symptom is still unconfirmed. If it recurs while the chat latency numbers look healthy, the cause is outside this chain.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Chat becomes trustworthy and diagnosable, which is the precondition for every other live test.
dependencies: One recorded protocol session (npm run protocol), step chat-still-answers-later

evidence.value: 20000, wraps every queued link including the confirmation deadline

proposals.title: Every simulated hostile attacks the same way, so damage trade-offs are not testable offline
proposals.explanation: Combat is now exercised offline: the simulated adapter equips a carried weapon like the live one, hostiles pursue inside an 8-block aggro radius, land a hit inside 1.6 blocks and die with drops, and a scenario gate reads the kills from the world. But `moveHostiles` gives every hostile the same numbers - 2 damage per hit, a 1 s cooldown, 2.6 blocks per second - whatever its name. A creeper does not explode, a skeleton never shoots, a spider is not faster, and armour or difficulty changes nothing. Scenarios can therefore test target choice, the health floor, withdrawal and kill confirmation, but not whether fighting a skeleton is worth more damage than fighting a zombie, which is what the engage/avoid table's ordering would need. The avoid list is still verified only as a choice, never against the harm it avoids.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Per-hostile damage and behaviour would let the engage/avoid table and the hit budget be justified by measurement instead of by reading vanilla tables.

evidence.value: 2, 1000 ms, 2.6 blocks per second for every hostile name
tests the choice only; the sim creeper does not explode

proposals.title: Nothing compares the simulated adapter with the live one, so a divergence passes as verified
proposals.explanation: The simulated adapter and `minecraft-adapter.ts` implement the same action contracts independently, and nothing compares them. On 2026-10-13 that produced a false green: the simulator's `attack()` read the weapon from the held slot only, while the live adapter calls `bestWeapon` over hand plus inventory and equips what it finds before the first swing. Every simulated fight was therefore refused with COMBAT_NO_WEAPON while the same run on a server would have fought, and `combat-opt-in-defence` still passed. Fixed by hand for that one action; the structural gap is untouched. Mining equips a carried pickaxe in both adapters, but no test says so, and the same class of divergence - preconditions, reach rules, confirmation semantics, failure codes - can appear in any action. Offline evaluation is the only measurement available without a server, so a divergence there quietly redefines what 'verified offline' means.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Offline results keep meaning what they say: a behaviour verified in the simulator was verified against the same preconditions the live adapter applies.

evidence.value: held slot only until 2026-10-13; now equips the best carried weapon
bestWeapon over hand plus inventory, then bot.equip before the first swing
none; minecraft-adapter.test.ts covers the live adapter alone

proposals.title: Stall detection exists for navigation only, not for combat or building
proposals.explanation: Navigation has `watchMovementProgress` and a sidestep recovery. Combat has a per-swing approach bound and already reports `hits` and `hitsConfirmed`, but nothing notices an engagement where three swings produced no `entityHurt` event. The build runners (`house-runner`, `excavation-runner`, `wheat-farm-runner`) have per-action timeouts of 5/20/30 s but no 'no block placed for N minutes' watchdog.
proposals.expectedBenefit: A fight or a build that makes no progress ends with a reason and a replan instead of running out its budget silently.

evidence.value: hitsConfirmed reported, never acted on
per action only

proposals.title: Leaving a sealed shelter is not a goal the planner can choose
proposals.explanation: `breakOutOfSealedShelter` in the adapter opens the two wall cells facing the navigation target, refuses unsafe ground beyond the wall and reads the result back — but it is only called from `executeNavigate`. An agent that is sealed and has no navigate candidate stays sealed, and nothing verifies it actually got out.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Getting out becomes an explicit skill with preconditions and an observed postcondition, which is also the precondition for the burrow strategy.

proposals.title: The shelter breakout has never run against a real server
proposals.explanation: Navigation runs with `canDig = false`, so the breakout is the only thing that can open a sealed shelter. Untested live questions: `bot.dig` on a stone wall without a pickaxe, whether the read-back sees the server's block state or client prediction, and whether pathfinder accepts the resulting one-block-wide opening. The offline double cannot answer any of them.

proposals.title: The observation carries no light level
proposals.explanation: `observation.ts` has no `light`, `skyLight` or `blockLight` field. Night is therefore only a tick number (`time.dayTicks`, `isNight`), and nothing can say whether the agent actually stands in the dark. That blocks light-driven torch placement and weakens the dusk decision, which currently has to guess from the clock.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Darkness becomes observable, which several survival decisions need.
dependencies: A schema change with its tests, and Mineflayer light access verified on a live server

evidence.value: no light level anywhere in the schema

proposals.title: Flee candidates only penalise unsafe cells instead of excluding them
proposals.explanation: `fleeCandidates` scores positions away from the threat centroid and subtracts `blocked * 1.5` for observed solid blocks on the route. Nothing excludes water, lava, fire or unobserved cells outright, so a flee can be scored as the best move into a hazard. The shelter planner already refuses unobserved cells; fleeing does not.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Running away stops being a way to die.

evidence.value: blocked cells penalised, hazards not excluded

proposals.title: Strafe sideways during a fight instead of only approaching or retreating
proposals.explanation: Combat movement is `approachForMelee` (close the gap) or withdraw. There is no lateral movement, although the sidestep geometry already exists for stall recovery (`recover:sidestep`, axis-aligned, never routing back across the stalled cell). Against a skeleton the approach is the expensive part, and against a spider it is the only way to avoid trading hits.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Fights cost less health, and ranged hostiles become answerable without a bow.

evidence.value: SIDESTEP_DISTANCE used for stall recovery only

proposals.title: Use a shield when one is carried
proposals.explanation: No shield handling exists anywhere in src. A shield would need off-hand equipping, raising and lowering around swings (blocking prevents attacking), and knowledge that axes disable shields briefly. Mineflayer's off-hand equip and activateItem behaviour has to be verified live before any of it can be trusted.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Frontal damage largely removed during an engagement, which is what makes the health floor reachable.
dependencies: Live verification of equip(off-hand) and activateItem

proposals.title: Eat on low health only when no hostile is close, with the limits unified
proposals.explanation: `needsFood` already fires at health <= 14 with hunger below the regen line, and one decision path checks for visible hostiles, but the health limit is a local constant and the 'no enemy close' precondition is not applied consistently or explained in the ledger. Vanilla also forbids eating at hunger 20, so 'eat when health is low' has to be stated as 'eat when health is low and eating is possible'.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Recovery is predictable and the decision log says why eating was skipped.

proposals.title: One configuration file for limits, time budgets and targets
proposals.explanation: Tuning numbers live in `survival-thresholds.ts`, `combat.ts`, `runtime-metrics.ts` (LOOP_TARGETS), the adapter config and `MINECRAFT_*`/`GAMEMIND_*` environment variables. There is no file an operator can edit, and no single place that reports the effective values. Waypoints deliberately stay out of this: homepoints are world data and already persist per world and dimension in `companion-memory.ts`.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Limits can be changed per server without a code change, and the effective configuration is inspectable.
dependencies: test/environment-settings.test.ts checks env names in both directions and has to move with this

evidence.value: code and README must not drift

proposals.title: Night behaviour depends on the companion mode, not only on the shelter
proposals.explanation: Operator intent: while following or after 'komm zu mir' the agent stays near the operator at night instead of locking itself away; on its own it should shelter. The modes already exist (`follow`, `come`, `guard`, `hold`, `task`) and so do homepoints for the morning return, but nothing makes the night decision mode-dependent, and an unverified `time.dayTicks` (a SessionField) has no conservative fallback.
proposals.expectedBenefit: The agent does not disappear at night while the operator called it, and does not stay out in the dark while working alone.

proposals.title: Start shelter preparation at dusk, scaled to the work remaining
proposals.explanation: `nightPressure` reports 'approaching' between dayTicks 12000 and the 13000 fallback for night — about 1000 ticks, roughly 50 seconds. Placing up to eight blocks plus walking does not reliably fit in that window. The lead time should be derived from the shortfall and the distance instead of being a fixed constant.
proposals.expectedBenefit: The shelter is closed before dark instead of during it.

evidence.value: 12000, about 50 s of real time

proposals.title: Scan the surroundings before leaving a shelter
proposals.explanation: The breakout already refuses lava, water, fire and unknown cells beyond the wall, but nothing checks hostiles, health, hunger or whether the first route cells are observed before the agent steps out. A single clearance check with its own refusal codes, coupled to the existing safety broker rather than duplicated beside it.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Leaving the shelter stops being the most dangerous moment of the night.

proposals.title: Report how many shelter blocks are missing, and what is short in the inventory
proposals.explanation: `planShelter` already returns `blocksNeeded` and a `skipped` list with reasons, and `placeableBlockCounts` counts what is carried — but `blocksNeeded` is used nowhere outside `shelter.ts`. The information exists and never reaches the operator.
proposals.expectedBenefit: The operator knows whether to drop blocks or wait, instead of watching a shelter that never closes.

evidence.value: blocksNeeded has no consumer

proposals.title: 'Meintest du?' for multi-word commands, from one shared vocabulary
proposals.explanation: `suggestMinecraftChatCommand` only suggests resource aliases, at six characters or more and within two edits. 'baue Starterhaus', 'plane Haus B', 'grabe 5x3x4', 'pflanze Weizenfeld' and 'folge mir' get no suggestion. The accepted vocabulary lives inside `parseMinecraftChatCommand`, so a suggester that re-lists it would drift.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Long commands become discoverable; the suggestion stays a question and never an action.

proposals.title: Chat reply texts in one module instead of inline templates
proposals.explanation: German and English replies are inline template strings inside a 1240-line controller, while the Control Center keeps its translations in `i18n-de.js`. Texts that two features need (the shelter shortfall, the suggestion question) cannot be shared or tested without touching the controller.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Reply texts become testable and reusable, which several interface proposals depend on.

proposals.title: Understand a duration in chat: 'hol uns Essen, ich komme in 5 Minuten wieder'
proposals.explanation: Chat parses counts ('noch 10') and dimensions ('grabe 5x3x4') but no durations, and no command carries a time budget from the operator. A bounded autonomous errand needs 'in 5 Minuten', '5 min' and 'eine Viertelstunde' plus a defined end state.
proposals.expectedBenefit: The operator can hand over a window of time instead of an open-ended task.

proposals.title: Hunt passive animals for food, separately from combat
proposals.explanation: Operator intent: while they are away, gather food from chickens, pigs and cows. `combatIsAllowed` refuses anything not on the hostile list by design, so this needs its own capability with its own rules: only cow, pig, chicken, sheep and rabbit; never players, villagers or tamed animals; a kill confirmed only by `entityDead`; drops collected with the existing pickup path. The safety rule that carries it is that hunting stops whenever a hostile is visible nearby, and never happens at night.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Food becomes something the agent can obtain on its own instead of only finding.

evidence.value: all entities within 24 blocks are already observed, so no schema change is needed

proposals.title: A time-boxed food errand with a defined end state and a report
proposals.explanation: 'Hol uns Essen, ich komme in 5 Minuten wieder' should end on its own: at the deadline or when the goal is met, hold position or return to the saved homepoint, then report what was gathered and where the agent is. `secure_food` already exists as a task kind with a target hunger and the eat/berry/pickup skills, so this extends it rather than adding a new task type.
proposals.expectedBenefit: The operator comes back to a result and a position, not to a bot that wandered off.

proposals.title: Furnace, fuel and smelting are not available
proposals.explanation: `furnace` appears in the useful-drop allowlist and in a progress-tracker description ('craft furnace, smelt iron, craft iron pickaxe'), but there is no smelting capability, no furnace recipe and no fuel handling. That blocks cooked food, iron tools and therefore armour.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Opens cooked food, iron tier and everything above it.

proposals.title: There is no way to obtain wool, so no bed
proposals.explanation: A bed needs three wool, and wool needs sheep or four string each. Sheep are passive, so the engage/avoid rules refuse them by design; shears need iron, which needs smelting. The remaining route is string from spiders, which are engageable — about twelve string for one bed. This has to be decided before any bed work starts.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Makes 'sleep through the night' either planable or consciously dropped.

proposals.title: Build a bed, place it and sleep through the night
proposals.explanation: Sleeping removes the whole class of night danger at once and stops phantoms from spawning after three sleepless nights. It needs a bed item, a placement rule for a two-block bed with a free approach, and Mineflayer's sleep call verified live. It also changes the night policy: the answer stops being 'hide' and becomes 'sleep'.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Nights stop costing time, shelter blocks and risk.

proposals.title: First day as one task: wood, table, stone tools, shelter
proposals.explanation: Operator intent for the first day: standard stone tools early, then shelter. The recipe knowledge is complete for it — planks, sticks, crafting table, wooden and stone pickaxe, axe, shovel and sword, with cobblestone as a mined ingredient — but nothing chains them into one objective with a report, and the bed the operator also mentioned is blocked by the wool question.
proposals.expectedBenefit: A new world reaches a safe, tooled state without step-by-step chat commands.

evidence.value: stone tools fully specified

proposals.title: Digging in as a third shelter strategy
proposals.explanation: Building a shelter costs eight placeable blocks; digging in costs one or two. It needs digging to be armed, observed solid and safe ground below (never straight down into lava, gravel or sand), a standable column, and a proven way out — navigation still runs with canDig false. Decided as a third strategy ('build', 'burrow', 'auto'), not a replacement, and only after the breakout is verified live.
proposals.expectedBenefit: A night shelter without a material run at dusk.

proposals.title: Place torches against night spawns
proposals.explanation: No torch recipe and no torch placement exist; coal is only tagged as useful for torches in the mining table. Without a light level in the observation, placement has to be heuristic — a ring at six to eight blocks around the shelter or work site — until light becomes observable.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Fewer hostiles spawning next to the shelter and the work area at night.

proposals.title: Observe and use armour
proposals.explanation: The observation carries equipment per slot but combat decisions only read the held item. Without armour in the decision, the combat floor has to be one flat number for every situation; with it, the floor can depend on what the agent is actually wearing, and armour itself becomes a craft worth planning.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Combat risk becomes a function of gear instead of a constant.

proposals.title: Record damage taken per engagement as roadmap evidence
proposals.explanation: `damageTaken` and `minHealth` are already collected for simulated runs, and combat outcomes already report hits, confirmed hits and the weapon. Writing damage per engagement into the episode evidence turns every combat tuning question — the health floor, strafing, shields — into a measured comparison instead of an argument.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Combat tuning decisions get numbers behind them.

proposals.title: Durability is observed but ignored in combat
proposals.explanation: Item stacks carry `durabilityUsed`, and `bestWeapon` picks by damage alone. A nearly broken sword is chosen like a new one, and the agent can end a fight unarmed mid-engagement with no replacement plan.
proposals.expectedBenefit: No fight is started on a weapon that will not survive it.

proposals.title: Store surplus in chests near the shelter
proposals.explanation: Storage blocks are already persisted per world in `companion-memory.ts` (up to 256 entries) but nothing uses them as an inventory overflow. A full 36-slot inventory stops gathering, and the drop path only removes junk.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Long gathering runs stop ending on a full inventory.

proposals.title: Return to the death position and recover the drops
proposals.explanation: The chat controller already keeps a death position, and the departure clearance and pickup paths would supply the rest. Nothing turns that position into a project with a scan before setting out and a report on arrival.
proposals.expectedBenefit: A death costs the items only if the agent cannot get back.

proposals.title: One line in the Control Center explaining why the agent is idle
proposals.explanation: The decision ledger already records why candidates were declined ('no_skill', 'threatened', 'no_budget', with the reason text). Nothing surfaces the most recent one as a single readable line, so an idle agent still looks unexplained at a glance.
proposals.expectedBenefit: The first question an operator asks is answered without reading a trace.

proposals.title: Split chat, combat and building into modules with their own tests
proposals.explanation: The adapter is 3574 lines and holds combat, navigation, breakout and swimming; the decision model is 2566 lines and holds every candidate family; the chat controller is 1240 lines and holds the gate, the interpreter, the approval state machine and task starts. Splitting has to be behaviour-preserving, with characterisation tests recorded first, and `failure-taxonomy.test.ts` and `environment-settings.test.ts` walk source directories, so moving files can break their assumptions.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Each behaviour becomes testable in isolation, which every feature above depends on.
dependencies: After the feature batches, so refactoring does not have to be rebased constantly

proposals.title: Remove unused functions, only from an operator-supplied list
proposals.explanation: Agreed rule: nothing is removed that the operator has not listed. The procedure per name is a repo-wide search including tests, docs, README, the Control Center's plain JavaScript and the Python launcher; re-exports; string references such as capability, skill and goal ids; and the two source-scanning tests. Optionally a report-only run of an unused-export tool, never an automatic deletion.
proposals.expectedBenefit: Less surface to misread, without losing something referenced only by a string.
dependencies: An explicit list of names from the operator

proposals.title: The Windows launcher CI job is red on main and on every branch
proposals.explanation: Every recent workflow run is red, main included: 'Launcher (Python, Windows 11 runner)' fails at `python -m unittest discover -s tests_py -t .` with exit code 1, while the same 53 tests pass on the Linux runner and the TypeScript job is green. Cause not established — the check annotations carry only 'Process completed with exit code 1' and the job log is not reachable from every environment. The tests are dependency-injected by design, so a plain platform assumption is unlikely; suspects are a Windows-specific path, process-liveness or port-binding assumption in launcher/checks.py, or the runner itself. Until this is green, CI cannot separate a real regression from the standing failure, which is why it outranks most feature work.
proposals.expectedBenefit: CI becomes a signal again: red means this change broke something.
dependencies: Access to the failing job log, or a Windows machine to run tests_py on
